included in award of Pension Credit Guarantee Credit

medication administered personally by a GP
mental disorder medication under a supervised community treatment order

mechanics: one charge per complete course of treatment, at the highest band needed
urgent/out-of-hours care costs one Band 1 charge even over several appointments
further treatment at the same band within two months is free
no charge if the dentist only issues a prescription or removes stitches

from 23 June 2026 contract changes: patients on the new complex-needs care pathway pay a single Band 2 charge unless Band 3 is also needed (per NHS England care pathways guidance; not independently verified)
exempt: pregnant or baby in previous 12 months
NHS inpatient treated by hospital dentist
income-related ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, qualifying Universal Credit (£435/£935)
dental.notExempt: Age 60+ is NOT a dental exemption in England

freeFor: told by an ophthalmologist you are at risk of glaucoma
40 or over and parent, sibling or child of a diagnosed glaucoma patient
registered severely sight-impaired/blind or sight-impaired/partially sighted
income-related ESA, Pension Credit Guarantee Credit, qualifying Universal Credit (£435/£935)
sight test done via a hospital eye department as part of managing an eye condition
sightTests.partialHelp: HC3 certificate may help with the cost of a private sight test

hospitalCareEntitlement.test: Free NHS hospital care depends on being 'ordinarily resident': 'living in the UK lawfully, voluntarily and for settled purposes'. Non-EEA nationals subject to immigration control must also have indefinite leave to remain (EEA/Swiss: settled or pre-settled status under EUSS). Nationality, tax paid or NI contributions do not decide it.
hospitalCareEntitlement.returningBritishCitizen: Entitled from the day of arrival if returning to resume settled residence: 'British citizens and non-UK nationals with ILR (or equivalent) who are returning to resume properly settled residence in the UK will most likely meet the ordinary residence test from the date of their arrival.' No minimum qualifying period. Proof of eligibility (at least 2 documents) is asked for at first treatment.
hospitalCareEntitlement.legalBasis: National Health Service (Charges to Overseas Visitors) Regulations 2015
hospitalCareEntitlement.freeToEveryone: A&E (A&E department, walk-in centre, minor injuries unit, urgent care centre) and GP/nurse primary care consultations are free to all regardless of residence; charges apply to other hospital care for those not ordinarily resident and not exempt.

immigrationHealthSurcharge.reducedAppliesTo: students, student dependants, Youth Mobility Scheme applicants, and applicants under 18 at application
immigrationHealthSurcharge.partYearRules: half the yearly amount for 6 months or less (applying from inside the UK); a full year's amount for more than 6 months but under a year
immigrationHealthSurcharge.effective: 2024-02-06 09:00 (rose from £624 and £470); still the rate on gov.uk as of 2026-09-29
immigrationHealthSurcharge.whatItBuys: use of the NHS in a similar way to an ordinarily resident person while the visa is valid, but prescription, dental and assisted-conception charges still apply

emergencyDepartmentCharge.rule: charged once per illness/accident at first ED visit without a GP referral letter; no charge with GP referral; follow-up outpatient visits for the same episode not charged again
exemptions: people admitted as in-patients from the ED
certain children's conditions listed in regulations
children referred from child health clinics/school exams
Hepatitis C Health Amendment Act card

injuryUnitChargeEUR.exempt: medical card or GP referral letter

publicOutpatient.rule: free as a public patient on GP referral

ireland.eligibility: Ordinarily resident in Ireland -> public in-patient and out-patient services in public hospitals; non-residents not otherwise covered pay full bed cost plus consultant.

gpVisit.rule: No set fees; private unless holder of medical card or GP visit card. Adults over 70 and children under 8 get a GP visit card.
gpVisit.note: Range is Citizens Information's stated typical expectation, not a regulated price; page last edited June 2024.

drugsPaymentScheme.unit: per household (adult, partner, children/dependants) per calendar month

imssBienestar.what: IMSS-BIENESTAR (OPD) provides medical care, medicines and associated supplies free of charge to people without social security (no IMSS/ISSSTE etc.).
imssBienestar.agreementText: Convenio de Coordinación ... para la prestación gratuita de servicios de salud, para las personas sin seguridad social en la Ciudad de México
imssBienestar.cdmxNetwork: 214 clinics, 39 UNEMEs, 22 second-level and 12 third-level hospitals across 14 operative regions (secondary report; not confirmed on an official page)
imssBienestar.registration: registro.imssbienestar.gob.mx; needs CURP, face photo, valid official ID, email and/or phone

uncertain: England 2025/26 dental figures rely on NHSBSA search snippets and the legislation title (SI 2025/310); the press-release body did not render. They match the April 2026 poster, which is consistent with a freeze.

HC12 p17 heads the prescription/PPC table 'from April 2025' although the leaflet is 'Effective from April 2026'; the gov.uk freeze announcement resolves this, but no single 2026 page was fetched that prints all three PPC figures under a 2026/27 heading.

Returning British citizen: guidance says 'will most likely meet the ordinary residence test from the date of their arrival' - a presumption, not an absolute; a return that is not 'properly settled' (e.g. a short visit) does not qualify.

Wales (1 April 2007) and Northern Ireland (1 April 2010) abolition dates are from general knowledge corroborated only loosely by the fetched official pages; Scotland's 1 April 2011 is from nhsinform's indexed text (direct fetch 403).
